finite_ar_main.description: Scaled finite-distribution analogue of the paper's main single-draft speculative decoding comparison. Block-efficiency references are finite benchmark values from the validated 80k-sample reproduction; total_variation=0.0 is the exact target-distribution ideal.
finite_ar_main.notes: The paper reports large-model Qwen2.5 results on GSM8K, HumanEval, and CNN/DailyMail. This gym deliberately uses exact finite autoregressive distributions to isolate verifier behavior under the same scientific objective; reference block-efficiency values therefore come from the validated finite reproduction, not from the paper tables.

block_efficiency.description: Generated tokens per serial target-model step. In train/test split scores this is support-normalized on the active slice so it stays in paper units while making the efficiency benefit held out without measuring wall-clock speed.

slice_block_efficiency.description: Generated tokens per serial target-model step attributable to the active train/test support slice, making the efficiency benefit split-sensitive without measuring wall-clock speed.

total_variation.description: Empirical total variation from the exact target sequence distribution, the losslessness constraint.

prefix_conditional_l1.description: Weighted next-token conditional L1 error on the active train/test prefix slice, catching local autoregressive shortcuts hidden by aggregate sequence mass.

slice_total_variation.description: Total-variation contribution on the active train/test support slice, used to detect distribution shortcuts that do not generalize across held-out sequence categories.

slice_mass_error.description: Absolute difference between empirical and exact target probability mass assigned to the active train/test support slice.

finite_ar_gamma3.description: Scaled finite-distribution draft-length ablation corresponding to the paper's draft-length study. Block-efficiency references are finite benchmark values from the validated 80k-sample reproduction; total_variation=0.0 is the exact target-distribution ideal.
finite_ar_gamma3.notes: The original paper varies draft length with large language models. This gym keeps the same type of stress test but uses a finite autoregressive setting; reference values are finite-benchmark values, not paper table values.
